description.narrative: Fideicomiso Irrevocable Numero 188156 (CFE Fibra E or the Issuer) is a publicly traded investment vehicle listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange. IFC proposes to invest up to US$150 million through the subscription of a 15-year, US$725 million amortizing bond. The Issuer will use the proceeds to acquire from CFE economic beneficiary rights to the distributions arising from the operation of the Mexican transmission network (RNT). These rights are held at, and will be acquired from, the Fideicomiso Irrevocable de Administración y Fuente de Pago No. 80758 (Promoted Trust). In turn, CFE will allocate these funds to support the modernization and expansion of the RNT. IFCs investment will be ring-fenced to a subset of projects that have been screened according to specific environmental and social (E&S) criteria.

The proposed main project outcomes are stakeholder effects through the improved quality of electricity supply and significant environmental benefits, both in climate change mitigation and adaptation. On the mitigation front, the project aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by minimizing technical losses, enhancing efficiency, and supporting greater integration of renewable energy sources. For climate adaptation, the project will bolster grid resilience against stressors such as heatwaves and hurricanes, which can disrupt voltage stability. Additionally, at the market level, the project seeks to increase sector resilience by facilitating private capital investment in the modernization and expansion of the transmission sector, a segment traditionally subject to limited private participation.

name.narrative: The proceeds from IFCs bond subscription will be used to support priority investments in Mexicos electricity transmission network that have been screened and deemed eligible under IFCs environmental and social (E&S) criteria. For details on the eligibility criteria, please refer to the Environmental and Social Review Summary (ESRS) linked to this projects SII on the IFCs project disclosure website. A subset of projects has been preliminarily screened and approved for investment under these criteria. From this group, specific projects will be selected for the use of IFC proceeds. These projects are located across Mexico, including the states of Baja California, Coahuila, Nuevo León, Chihuahua, Puebla, Morelos, Ciudad de México, Sonora, Tamaulipas, Durango, and Jalisco.
